decisions.reason: The same-message MODIFY already records that the Hero V remains the signature reference while the optically drawn second V uses a right arm matched optically to it; the approved Hero V geometry itself remains unchanged.

The existing message-177 MODIFY already replaces mathematical scaling with optical drawing, records the alphabet relationship and extended right arm, and removes the obsolete proportional-scaling attributes.

The current signature-sweep rule exempts the second V specifically because it was a proportional reduction; the new direction preserves that exception through an optically matched extended right arm instead.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I’d like us to change direction: please reset the design around our original Hero V, which I still consider the strongest version, and stop scaling the second V mathematically. From that anchor, explore an optically drawn second V instead. It should share the alphabet’s design language and DNA while naturally serving as a supporting form. Keep the extended right arm as the signature detail, matching it optically to the Hero V, but achieve that result through drawing rather than pure scaling.

Looking back through the earlier proofs and these explorations clarified the problem. Although the reduction is technically proportional, the resulting V appears to belong to a different alphabet; mathematical reduction causes it to lose some of the character and presence that make the Hero V so compelling.

I’m attaching my current favorite image as the preferred reference, though it lacks the desired right-arm extension. Taking this optical approach should produce a more cohesive, timeless wordmark in which every letter feels deliberately crafted instead of mechanically derived.

value_updates.signature_sweep_usage: The expressive Hero V gesture remains excluded from the E and L forms; the optically drawn second V retains an extended right arm matched optically to the Hero V while sharing the alphabet’s design language and DNA.

decisions.reason: The second V is no longer a locked proportional asset within the composition; the client explicitly reopens it for optical drawing while retaining the original Hero V as the anchor.

The requested cohesive and timeless result is consistent with the existing brand-expression state and introduces no new or changed brand-expression rule.
The source changes construction of the second V but does not alter the wordmark-led identity, the absence of a separate icon, or the opening V’s standalone role.
